column2: Act Seven
The Feast of Dragons
Dragons'Feast
He slowly raised the lid, his voice full of mysterious enticement. “A weapon out of legend... a set of alchemical blades!”
A sharp, dark-golden light flowed through the widening gap. Lu Mingfei froze. Suddenly he felt that the thing inside the case was alive; he could hear a familiar breathing sound coming from within.
The lid opened. Alchemical blades? The Seven Deadly Sins! It was like meeting an old friend again.

Lu Mingfei opened his sleepy eyes. The room was silent. He turned his head. The sheet where Chu Zihang had slept was perfectly smooth, without so much as a depression, while Xia Mi's blanket was neatly folded, as though it had never been opened.
“Some friends,” he muttered.

Had those two gone out to have fun first thing in the morning without even telling him? He stared at the ceiling for a while, then wondered whether Xia Mi might have a thing for Chu Zihang. Come to think of it, the beautiful freshman and the expressionless senior admired by everyone yet always single did make a good match. They even had common ground academically, which was to say neither of them spoke like a normal human being. Still, it wouldn't have hurt to take him along. He might always be a third wheel, but he was a considerate one: a good light bulb that didn't flash at random, just cast a warm glow on the couple beside him.
It was so quiet, as though he were the only person left in the world.

Lu Mingfei suddenly felt strange, uncertain where he was. There was no evidence that he was still dreaming or had woken up. On a morning like this, waking alone in an unfamiliar place was itself like a dream, wasn't it?

He had always had a weak presence, but never felt so unmoored. Lying on the soft bed, he seemed to float in the air. Aunt must really be angry this time. Would he go back to Uncle's next summer? If he did, Aunt would glare at him again. But if he didn't, where could he go? Stay on an empty campus? Everyone else would go home for summer vacation, leaving him all alone. Without Chu Zihang, Caesar, Nono, Xia Mi, and Fingel, he really was on his own. Was this what they called blood sorrow? Or the loneliness the devil version of Lu Mingze spoke about?
Thinking of Lu Mingze, he paused. Then he understood.
“Breakfast!” He clapped imperiously.
The door opened, and Lu Mingze pushed in a gleaming silver food cart. He was not much taller than the cart, but wore a proper white chef's uniform and a tall French chef's hat.

“I've just woken up and I'm terribly tired. His Majesty will dine in bed. Bring it over.” Lu Mingfei put on a grand air, reclining against his pillows like a French noblewoman awakened from a springtime nap.

“Caviar with freshly toasted whole-wheat bread, raisin Danish pastry, chicken breast sautéed with lemon juice, and grilled Munich white sausage.” Lu Mingze spoke with the exacting attentiveness of a butler. “To drink, would you prefer coffee, milk and cereal, or kiwi juice?”
“That's all? His Majesty's favorites are fried dough sticks and soft tofu pudding!”

“No problem.” Lu Mingze lifted the silver cloche to reveal a set of white Chinese porcelain, four perfectly fried dough sticks, two bowls of silky soft tofu pudding, and several side dishes: Gaoyou salted duck eggs, Jinhua ham, Hangzhou vegetarian chicken, and Wangzhihe fermented tofu in chili oil.
As for the caviar, Danish pastry, chicken breast, and grilled sausage he had just mentioned, there was no sign of any of them.

“Are you messing with me? Four fried dough sticks and two bowls of tofu pudding, and you pretend to be a French chef?” That was what Lu Mingfei said, but he was happy. Once he returned to Cassell College he would have nothing but German food: endless sausages, sauerkraut, and pork knuckles.

“Our customer service is first-rate. A magic breakfast: if French breakfast had been what you wanted, that's exactly what you'd have found under the cover.” Lu Mingze sat on the edge of the bed. “You only get two dough sticks and one bowl of tofu pudding. The other half is mine.”

Lu Mingfei hesitated. “Am I eating in a dream? In reality, am I chewing on toads and drinking foot-washing water? It happens in Journey to the West: the White Bone Demon turns into a village girl bringing food, but the food is really toads, clods of dirt, and broken roof tiles.”

“Of course not. You're a customer, and customers are the greatest. We devils always treat our customers well. We're businesspeople! Hard work brings prosperity!” Lu Mingze lifted a bowl of tofu pudding, blew on it, and took a sip. “Satisfied?”

“Satisfied, my foot! You've got too many tricks. I can't beat you, so I give up!” Unable to resist the fragrance of the fried dough, Lu Mingfei grabbed a stick and took a bite. It was superb, crisp and rich with oil. Even if it turned out to be a toad in the real world, he would accept it.

“Get to the point. I didn't summon you this time, so don't put it on my account,” Lu Mingfei mumbled. A big spoonful of tofu pudding brought a hint of heat, and it tasted exactly like the breakfast stall outside his uncle's home.
Tofu pudding like this was reason enough to keep muddling through this lonely world!
“Of course. That was settled when we made the contract.” Lu Mingze sounded magnanimous. “Something's going to happen today. I came especially to let you know, so you don't make a mistake.”
“Something's going to happen?” Lu Mingfei frowned and picked up a piece of vegetarian chicken with his chopsticks.
“You have an important event coming up that will require money. I know you're a poor dog, so I'm going to lend you some.”
“No!” Lu Mingfei refused without hesitation.
“No?” Lu Mingze was surprised.

“Borrow money from you? That means asking you for help, doesn't it? Asking you costs me part of my life. No deal! I don't need money for anything. If kidnappers came after me, I'd be better off summoning you to knock them all down. That would cost the same quarter of my life.”
“It's a complimentary gift for a customer. No charge.”
“You? So kind?” Lu Mingfei eyed Lu Mingze sideways.

“Me.” Lu Mingze smiled. On the little devil's face, the innocent smile was like green leaves in the morning light. Even knowing how full of wicked schemes he was, you couldn't hate him when he smiled like that.
“In this whole world, I'm the only one who's always of one mind with you. Because... you're my brother.” He actually reached out and gently touched Lu Mingfei's forehead.
“What are you touching me for? You've smeared chili oil on my face!” Lu Mingfei shouted.

But the instant Lu Mingze's hand touched his forehead, he felt an indescribable warmth. It was not merely the warmth of a hand that had held a bowl of tofu pudding; a tangible current of warmth flowed from Lu Mingze's palm into his body. The simple, natural touch felt as though it had happened thousands, tens of thousands of times in dreams: a hand touching his forehead, saying... Brother.

Looking back, this sneaky big boy had never harmed him once. Whenever he was at the end of his rope, with no answer from heaven or earth, and Caesar, Nono, and Chu Zihang could do nothing to help, only this devil version of Lu Mingze had stayed by his side. As long as he was willing to make a deal, Lu Mingze would help him, like the person closest to him in the whole world.

“This time's temporary Yanling is ‘show me the money.’ In StarCraft, entering that cheat code gives you ten thousand minerals and gas. This Yanling adds ten thousand US dollars to your assets, and you can use it repeatedly.” Lu Mingze withdrew his hand.

“I reward my customers so often. Couldn't you summon me for something important once in a while?” He jumped off the bed and walked softly to the door, then turned back. “But I expect you will soon. Danger isn't far away. Stay alert and keep that phone with you at all times. Text me if anything happens. Oh, and someone left a note for you at the front desk. I brought it up on my way. It's on the cart.”
He closed the door behind him.
The lock clicked shut. Lu Mingfei gave a start, and everything returned to normal.

It was still the same hotel room, with the same warm morning light coming through the sheer white curtains, but the details had changed. A depression where Chu Zihang had slept appeared beside Lu Mingfei; the blanket on Xia Mi's bed was a mess, not folded at all. Orange peels lay scattered on the table. Xia Mi's white cotton pajamas hung over the back of a chair, with a yellow sticky note attached: “Senior Mingfei, we had to go out on an errand. We ordered you a Chinese breakfast: fried dough sticks and tofu pudding.” A cat's head was drawn in place of a signature. Xia Mi actually signed with a cat's head.
With those subtle changes, the dreamlike feeling, the sense of being a stranger to the world, vanished.

The food cart was still there. Soft, white tofu pudding remained in the bowl, sprinkled with fragrant chili-sesame oil, shreds of preserved mustard greens, shrimp, sesame, and dark vinegar. Half a fried dough stick lay on the plate, still steaming. This time Lu Mingze really hadn't tricked him.
Suddenly he felt like crying, though he didn't know why... and he also wanted to sneeze...

Lu Mingfei drew a deep breath and let out an earth-shaking sneeze, tears streaming down his face. If the tears had come from grief, his sorrow must have been as vast as the sea. But they didn't. They came from a streak of red sauce spread on the dough stick.
Blazingly hot bird's-eye chili sauce!

“Damn you! Who eats fried dough sticks with bird's-eye chili sauce? Lu Mingze, you're vicious!” Lu Mingfei wiped away his tears and imagined he could hear the sly little devil laughing triumphantly after going out the door.

“If I ever trust him again, I'm his son!” Lu Mingfei swore inwardly as he came out of the bathroom, wiping his mouth. Lu Mingze had spread the chili sauce as thickly as peanut butter. He had spent ten minutes frantically rinsing his mouth with cold water.

“If breakfast was a prank... then the money-making Yanling probably can't be trusted either, right?” Lu Mingfei thought. Besides, how was he supposed to use it? Shout “show me the money” into the air and have a courier deliver a package of cash? It could supposedly be used repeatedly. If he shouted it a hundred times, that would be a million dollars. Would an armored truck pull up outside the hotel?
A pale-yellow envelope lay on the food cart. In beautiful script it was addressed to “Ricardo M. Lu.”
“Dear Ricardo:

This is a mission notice. Please go downstairs immediately upon receiving it. A black Maserati sedan will be waiting outside the hotel, with Illinois license plate ‘CAS001.’ The person in the car will explain the details of the mission.”

The letter was printed on Hyatt stationery. If not for the seal at the bottom, Lu Mingfei would have assumed it was another of Lu Mingze's pranks. The security emblem was used exclusively by Cassell College; the last time he had seen one was on his disastrous transcript.
Lu Mingfei ran out of the hotel and immediately spotted the black Maserati parked at the curb.

It was a prestigious car sold alongside Ferraris. The long hood curved sharply, like a shark leaping from the water, while privacy glass blocked any view inside. Definitely a stylish toy. Lu Mingfei craned his neck, trying to see who was in it. He had heard the Executive Department paid very well, but who could be wealthy enough to drive a Maserati on a mission?

A tailored black suit? Gleaming Italian leather shoes? Hair so heavily oiled it could serve as a mirror? Dragons must be a terribly conceited race, if even their hybrid descendants loved showing off so much. Nine out of ten men and women at the college put on aristocratic airs. Even Chu Zihang drove a Panamera on official business. Or was it a beautiful woman? A qipao slit all the way to the top of the thigh, slender high heels, long waves of hair? No, that outfit belonged exclusively to female Nationalist spies... Lu Mingfei's imagination ran wild.
The car door popped open automatically and nearly hit him in the head. He ducked inside.

A tailored black suit, gleaming Italian leather shoes, hair oiled to a mirror shine, and a vivid red rose on the chest. If the man hadn't had a head of silver hair, he'd have looked like a thoroughgoing lecher! Add the silver hair and he was... an old lecher!
“P-Pr... Principal!” Lu Mingfei stammered.

“Hello, Mingfei. Let's work together wholeheartedly on this mission.” Anjou smiled and raised his glass. The old man clearly knew how to enjoy life. A lilting aria played on the stereo; the slot that should have held a Coke contained a bottle of ice wine instead. The sunroof stood open overhead, and delicate curls of cigar smoke drifted upward.
“You... got stranded in Chicago by the strike too?” Lu Mingfei felt a small, involuntary thrill. He wasn't the only unlucky one.

“You could say that, although I planned to stay here for two days anyway to attend an auction.” Anjou handed him a beautifully printed brochure. “Sotheby's, one of the world's finest auction houses, is an important marketplace for art.”

Lu Mingfei was bewildered. An auction? That was something rich young masters like Caesar played at. What did it have to do with him? The college's mission... could they be going to rob the auction house? Possible! The Executive Department was hardly made up of saints; they seemed to have broken plenty of laws and rules. Maybe the sports car was for a fast getaway. But if they really were robbing an auction house, shouldn't they send someone tough like Chu Zihang? Instead they were sending a man who was actually over a hundred years old with a novice? Granted, the old man's Yanling and fighting skills seemed no worse than a young man's, but what if a stray bullet happened to take out the principal...

He leafed through the brochure. China really had prospered: it was printed in Chinese too. A Qing Qianlong doucai tripod dish in the form of a mallow flower with floral motifs... a Song blue-and-white, underglaze-red high-necked vase with a low-relief design of the Music of the Prince of Qin Breaking the Battle Formation... a great Nanyang Dushan jade vessel depicting Vairocana Buddha with lowered hands... The elaborate names bloomed one after another, with startling prices beneath them.

“The items in the brochure aren't what interest us.” Anjou waved his cigar. “This is a restricted auction: an auction of objects that the law permits to circulate only within certain limits, so only clients of particular standing are invited. But objects offered at such auctions often have obscure origins, and even major auction houses don't dare publicize them. They invite only discreet, trustworthy clients. In 2003 Sotheby's tried to auction six pottery figures from the tomb of Empress Dou of the Western Han. They were stolen relics, and it caused quite a stir. Since then, certain interesting objects haven't been printed in promotional materials. You have to attend in person to see what's revealed.”

“So... we really are going there to bid?” Lu Mingfei relaxed. Watching Anjou wave his cigar, he had kept imagining the old man pulling a loaded Colt pistol out of the glove compartment, tossing it to him, and saying, “Today's job is up to the two of us!”
“Of course.” Anjou looked surprised. “One goes to an auction to bid on things.”
“Good, good. Please go on, Principal.” Lu Mingfei nodded vigorously.

“Restricted auctions are where the college hunts for treasures. We often find obscure pieces. For example, we once paid less than four hundred thousand dollars for a brass blowtorch of unknown age. Do you know the kind?” Anjou gestured with both hands. “An alcohol blowtorch like chemists used in the century before last.”
“I've seen one. Only the teacher was allowed to use it in high-school lab. It's like a little flamethrower.”
“Quite right. Now imagine turning the blowtorch sideways...”
“Then... it's a flamethrower!” Lu Mingfei understood.

“Exactly! It wasn't an alcohol blowtorch at all, but a weapon made by a nineteenth-century alchemical technician. They usually called such things ‘dragon's breath.’ The fuel wasn't alcohol, but refined mercury-bearing nitroglycerin.”
“Nitroglycerin... isn't that an explosive?”

“Correct. An explosive. It could project a cone of flame twenty meters long, with an explosive effect, while releasing enormous quantities of mercury vapor. A powerful weapon against dragons.” Anjou nodded. “That's why I say it's a place to find treasures.”
“And I'm going because...”

“You'll play a buyer new to the trade. There's an item we want you to bid on for us.” Anjou handed him a wireless earpiece. “It's simple. Just follow my instructions. But remember, at the auction you and I don't know each other.”
“I don't think I'm suitable... I don't know anything about auctions...” Lu Mingfei lost his nerve.

“That doesn't matter. The college will create all kinds of opportunities for you to learn.” Anjou drew deeply on his cigar and was silent for several seconds. “You're the only S-rank student at the college now. You have a great deal to learn. While the Night Watcher and I can still protect this school, you must learn as quickly as you can... There's not much time.”
“Not... much time?” Lu Mingfei heard a deep loneliness in the old man's words.

“At my age, how much longer do you think I can live?” Anjou shrugged. “I was among the earliest members of the Lionheart Society. Of course, if you'd lived through the entire twentieth century, you wouldn't care much about whether you died either.”

“And yet... you smoke so much...” Lu Mingfei stammered. He had never imagined that someone as formidable as the principal could die. To any Cassell student, the principal and the Night Watcher were the foundations of the school. An old man who had lived 130 years and could still leap like a tiger with a folding knife and stab a Dragon King through the head was practically an ancient monster! And weren't ancient monsters supposed to live for a thousand years? Hearing one speak about a subject as serious as death was both funny and sad.

“The advantage of dragon genes is that most of us will never get cancer. Many fatal diseases leave us alone. If I die one day, it will be because every part of me has worn out... or because a Dragon King's Yanling blows my head apart.” The old man casually flicked the cigar butt through the sunroof, gripped the wheel with one hand, and floored the accelerator.

The dangerous shark roared away, ignoring the changing traffic light and plunging into the stream of cars. Several vehicles behind it braked in panic, blocking the entire intersection at crooked angles.

“Hey, hey, hey!” Lu Mingfei hadn't even had time to fasten his seat belt and could only cling desperately to the handhold. The acceleration that car magazines praised so highly was torture now, like an immense force pinning him to the seat.

These Cassell College lunatics! No wonder the old saying went that when the upper beam was crooked, the lower ones would lean too. Compared with this, Chu Zihang merely reversed at sixty kilometers an hour. What a law-abiding driver!
Anjou drained his glass of ice wine with pleasure and kept accelerating. Evidently the old man drove fast as a matter of course.

Ice wine? Wait, no. Ice wine had no business here, did it? They were already going 120 kilometers an hour, and the old man driving had a stemmed glass in his hand? This was too much excitement. Lu Mingfei's head buzzed.
“Principal... driving after drinking, in China...” Lu Mingfei swallowed hard. “They revoke your license for that!”

“Same in America.” Anjou shrugged. “But do you think they'd renew a license for a 130-year-old man? When I learned to drive, there was no such thing as a driver's license. That was 1899... yes, 1899. Cars had only been invented in 1885, a new toy that couldn't outrun a carriage yet. No Ford, no General Motors, no traffic rules at all!”

“Principal, you've... been driving without a license for over a hundred years?” Lu Mingfei's heart nearly leaped into his throat. A moment ago, passing another car, he'd been sure they would crash; the gap was so narrow it was like two Japanese swordsmen crossing blades, their quick swords flashing past each other in midair. “Principal, I'm still young! I want to live a good long life!”
“That's right.” Anjou smiled. “You're still young. But remember what I just told you? I don't know how much time I have left...”
“Hey, please! Could you stop accelerating when you change the subject?”

“I haven't changed it. I mean... as an old man with one foot in the grave who loves driving fast, what do I have left to lose?” Anjou switched the gear setting to that damned super-sport mode and let out a whoop that would have sent a teenage girl's hormones racing.
The Maserati slowed and stopped at the curb.
“Ready? The mission is about to begin. Remember your identity? You're Lu Mingfei, an art enthusiast from China...” Anjou handed him a cigar sealed in an aluminum tube.

“I've memorized it. I'm Lu Mingfei, a nouveau riche bumpkin who's fallen for a girl at art school and wants to cultivate some artistic taste... Damn it, I've finally made it to an amazing auction, and I'm going to pick up some good stuff for my mansion with the water feature! I don't know how to smoke fancy things like cigars. I don't smoke cigarettes either.” The mission plan had included his cover story, which Lu Mingfei now knew backward. He imagined himself an actor, trying hard to get into character.
“You don't have to know how. Just hold it in your mouth and draw. You're attending an auction; you need an expensive habit or two to show your worth. This is a Cuban cigar, fifty dollars apiece!”
“Very nouveau riche.” Lu Mingfei held the cigar in his mouth like a grilled sausage.
“That's why I chose you instead of Chu Zihang or Caesar. You're better at playing a nouveau riche upstart.”
“True. I'm a bumpkin.”

Anjou handed him an envelope. “Your invitation is inside. Keep it safe. You need a two-million-dollar deposit in your account. Norma opened an account for you at a bank in Zurich and deposited two million.”
“Wow! Two million!” Lu Mingfei imagined that if he looked in a mirror, dollar signs would be rolling across his wide-open eyes.
“It's mission funding. It will be withdrawn from your account afterward.”

“I don't care if it lasts forever; I only care that I have it today.” The ridiculous line rolled out of Lu Mingfei's mouth without passing through his brain. “But Principal, you're such a tasteful man, and clearly rich. Why not bid for it yourself?”

“An auction is a psychological game. Especially with rarities seldom seen on the market: no one can assess their value at once, and psychology becomes particularly important. An artwork's price depends on how many people want it. The more bidders, the higher the price rises. If an experienced buyer bids aggressively, many will follow, driving it up. And I am an experienced buyer. Almost everyone there knows me.”
“So if you raise your paddle, it tells them the thing is valuable?” Lu Mingfei nodded. “In plain language, I'm a plant.”

Anjou gave him a thumbs-up. “Exactly, you're a plant! I'll bid on a few small things for appearances, but I won't raise my paddle for the real target. I want it to seem an obscure item no one cares about. You will bid, and everyone will think that new rich upstart is spending his money on something useless, while you get it cheaply.”

“Understood!” Lu Mingfei said. “By the way, Principal, do you know where Chu Zihang went? We also met a freshman named Xia Mi yesterday. We shared a room last night, and when I woke up they were both gone.”

“Norma arranged another assignment for Chu Zihang. He's showing Xia Mi around Chicago and giving her pre-enrollment orientation at the same time. Usually a professor would do it, but since we have an extra seven days, we should make good use of them.” Anjou thought for a moment. “I believe they went to Six Flags, the roller-coaster park.”
“No way! I've never been to Six Flags either... I want to take a pretty junior on a roller coaster too!” Lu Mingfei failed to stop himself; his true feelings spilled out.
Anjou stared for a moment, then said awkwardly, “I'm the principal. I'm more important than a pretty junior... Students would firmly turn down a date just to have afternoon tea with me...”
“At your age, why are you competing with a girl for attention?” Lu Mingfei shrugged.
“Get out!”
“Hey... is this about a man's pride? Isn't that a bit much?” Lu Mingfei stared wide-eyed.

“You're a plant. Naturally you can't appear with me. Someone will pick you up here shortly. Remember to change: a full Armani outfit, the brand all wealthy Chinese bumpkins love. Walk with your chest out. You're a man coming here to spend two million dollars; look down on everything. Don't overestimate those well-dressed Sotheby's auctioneers. They're just people earning a commission.” Anjou clapped him hard on the shoulder. “You failed two courses last semester...”

“Hey, Principal, that's unfair. Don't bring up a sore subject... How am I supposed to act arrogant when you remind me of that?” Lu Mingfei made a miserable face, and the cigar fell from his mouth onto the seat.
“I mean that as principal I have the authority to give you extra credit. If you perform this assignment beautifully, I'll give you passing grades.” Anjou held out his hand. “Deal?”
“You can do that? Deal!” Lu Mingfei's fighting spirit blazed at once, and he seized Anjou's hand.
“I told you hanging around the principal had a brighter future than hanging around a pretty junior...”
“...You're not still bothered by what I said, are you?”

“Of course not. I'm always magnanimous...” Anjou took out a jet lighter and lit the thick cigar for Lu Mingfei. “Now smoke your Cohiba, wear your Armani suit, and go do battle in the arena of wealth, our young Chinese millionaire!”
The car door flew open. The principal lifted a foot and kicked the stunned Lu Mingfei out. The Maserati sped away in a cloud of dust.
“Hey! So violent? You really were embarrassed and angry, weren't you?” The young upstart Lu Mingfei pounded the pavement and shouted after the disappearing car.

His stomach gave an unhelpful rumble, wiping away his anger. Only then did he remember he'd eaten just half his breakfast. He got up helplessly, dusted himself off, and rolled his eyes toward the sky. It was clear and freshly washed, and a white-winged gull that had strayed from Lake Michigan into the human city glided among the skyscrapers.

Pennsylvania Avenue was a small road hidden in the busy downtown district, with the towering gray walls of skyscrapers on either side. The buildings dated from Chicago's most luxurious metropolitan era, the 1950s. Over the years their limestone surfaces had flaked away, giving them the forlorn air of fallen nobility. The tall buildings blocked out all sunlight, leaving a chill in the long, narrow street. At the end stood a massive square building, its high walls windowless except for a row of large ventilation fans turning slowly near the top.
The Chicago Civic Opera House.

It had once been a gathering place for celebrities. Sixty years ago, every night brought luxury cars and fashionable women. Courteous gentlemen escorted young companions to enjoy refined music, while attendants called out the names of distinguished guests.
But its glory had faded. Young people now went on dates to movie theaters or shopping centers downtown. The opera house belonged to the splendor of another age.

Today it had awakened again. A succession of luxury cars stopped at the entrance, red taillights flashing one after another. Heavy doors opened, and men in black tailcoats or evening suits stepped out, all wearing white embroidered shirts and metropolitan side parts slicked with enough oil to shine like mirrors. Hands in long white velvet gloves emerged from the cars, silver watches worn outside the gloves. The men took those hands and lightly helped out fashionable women wrapped in mink and veils, slender heels touching the pavement, calves drawn into graceful curves. White steam rose from sewer grates, and the men and women walking arm in arm toward the opera house formed a picture of Chicago in the golden age of 1950.
Outside the Civic Opera House that day, time seemed to have flowed backward sixty years.

A black Lincoln sedan drew slowly to the entrance. Its old-fashioned grandeur caught an attendant's eye, and he hurried down the steps. The window lowered, and a young, long-fingered hand with prominent joints held out a dark-red invitation.
“Mr. Ricardo M. Lu!” the attendant called the unfamiliar name as though welcoming a well-known count.

The driver got out, his back perfectly straight, dressed in black with gold-plated buttons. He respectfully opened the rear door. A young man with pale-gold hair emerged and swept a cool gaze over the passing guests. His upright figure stood in the wind like a spear planted in the ground. He put on black sunglasses, hiding his handsome face, and pulled back his striped shirt cuff to glance at a fine IWC watch.
“This way, Mr. Lu. The auction is about to begin.” The attendant bowed to the young guest of honor.
The guest waved him away coolly, turned, and went to a silver extended Bentley behind the Lincoln. Bending slightly, he opened its door. “This way, Mr. Lu.”
The flamboyant display shocked every passing guest. So this imposing young man was... the one who opened the car door!

This time the first thing to appear was a thick Cohiba cigar, then an expensive custom Armani suit, then a snow-white lace cravat, then polished Ferragamo shoes. Surprise spread over every face as the honored guest finally emerged in full. He drew a breath, thrust out his chest, and looked down on the assembled company, a brown Burberry trench coat draped over his shoulders. He took a deep drag on the cigar...
Then erupted in violent coughing. The blond young man hurried over to pat his back. Around them came a ripple of snickers of uncertain meaning.

“Damn it!” Lu Mingfei cursed inwardly. There was nothing wrong with this outfit. What were they laughing at? He'd only choked on the cigar! Besides, hadn't his entrance imitating Mark Gor been impressive?

“They're laughing because you've put on every fashionable designer label at once. Your taste is too mixed. Ignore them. That's your assigned role.” Anjou's low voice sounded in his ear. In his nervousness, Lu Mingfei had almost forgotten the wireless earpiece.
“What kind of lousy role is this...” A tiny microphone was hidden beside Lu Mingfei's jaw.
“Whatever you see, don't show surprise. Just follow along.” Anjou was hidden somewhere out of sight.

Lu Mingfei followed the attendant through a dim passage, perfume drifting faintly in the air. The glints came from silver powder on the fashionable women's bare shoulders. The luxurious, unreal surroundings made him a little dizzy. Then the space ahead brightened.
Suddenly he emerged into a vast open space, as if golden light were shining from every direction.

The opera house spread out before him, a wave of splendor washing over him. Towering columns all around resembled the ruins of the Parthenon on the Acropolis, but painted a magnificent dark red. Beneath the domed ceiling, enormous crystal chandeliers banished every shadow. The dome and walls, golden in the light, were painted with the battles of Ragnarök. A wool carpet bore green mandala designs; brass plates marked the numbers on red velvet seats. A scarlet curtain hung over the stage, as though drawing it back would reveal a tragedy by some ancient Greek master.
He didn't have enough eyes to take it all in and didn't know where to look. Amid the endless crowd, he felt lost.

He found his seat, but not Anjou. Guests settled into the surrounding seats, exchanging brief greetings as though they all knew one another. The opera house was not very large, but all several hundred seats were occupied.

The lights went out one by one until only the huge branching chandelier in the center of the dome remained lit. As if a performance were about to begin, white-clad attendants passed through the aisles ringing a string of bells, and the guests' conversations died down. The curtain trembled, and a man in a black tailcoat stepped out.

“Ladies and gentlemen, Sotheby's restricted auction, the 2010 Summer Chicago Cultural Journey sale, will begin in five minutes. I am your auctioneer. Please keep hold of your paddles and don't miss the things you desire, because every item we're about to offer is unique.” He paused. “Now, night has fallen. Please close your eyes.”
What was this? Lu Mingfei stared. Were they playing a murder game? Did they have to close their eyes at night and open them at dawn? The guests all closed their eyes and lowered their heads slightly.
“Day has broken. Please open your eyes!”

Everyone opened their eyes at once. For an instant it was as though the opera house had lit up again, but this time it was not crystal chandeliers illuminating the hall. It was hundreds of pairs of golden eyes!
Lu Mingfei felt his heart stop.
“Don't move or say anything. Don't look around,” Anjou's voice sounded in his ear.
“But that's... that's... that's...” Lu Mingfei almost groaned.

“Yes, genuine golden eyes, every one. This isn't a masquerade. They're revealing their golden eyes to show their bloodlines. Everyone attending this auction is a hybrid, like you and me. This is...” Anjou paused. “A feast of dragons!”
Lu Mingfei was thankful there was still a chair beneath him. Otherwise he would have collapsed like an overcooked noodle and wet himself.

What kind of place was this? The hall was full of distinguished guests, every one a human-dragon hybrid! Gold cards, platinum cards, and black cards didn't signify status here. Everyone displayed golden eyes as proof of bloodline. But he... he was staring in terror, eyes almost popping out, red as a little white rabbit's.

A feast of dragons? A grand name for a bunch of half-dragons throwing a party in a dragon's den, right? There had to be a main course. Were these people vegetarians? He was the only little white rabbit here!
“May I get past?” a low, cool voice said beside him.

Lu Mingfei turned and sucked in a breath. A pair of golden eyes shone beside him like lamps. They belonged to a young man in his twenties who had arrived late. Before Lu Mingfei could look away, their eyes met. We're doomed! I've been exposed, he thought. If he'd known what kind of gathering this was, he should have brought gold cosmetic contacts. In this sea of golden eyes, he was like a green-eyed foreigner sitting in a Chang'an tavern at the height of the Tang dynasty. How could anyone fail to see he was different?
Sure enough, the man paused, and the light in his pupils grew fiercer, as if golden blades were gathering in his eyes.
Lu Mingfei went rigid. That piercing gaze! In an anime, it would surely come just before a devastating special attack!
“Very understated,” the man said suddenly with an appreciative click of his tongue. The gold in his pupils dimmed slightly, and he held out a hand in friendship. “Romario Townsend. Call me Roma.”
Understated, my ass! It's just that I can't make my eyes turn gold, brother! Lu Mingfei shook his hand nervously.

“Ever since auctions like this began, people have lit their golden eyes to show off the purity of their bloodlines and put pressure on others when they meet their gaze,” Townsend said, sitting beside Lu Mingfei and lowering his voice. “Eventually everyone started doing it, and it turned into a masquerade. But it's hard not to follow the crowd. Bloodline is what matters here, as if without golden eyes yours won't even be recognized.” Townsend scoffed. “I think your way is better: natural, relaxed. We're here for things we like, after all. Spending money should be fun. Keeping golden eyes lit for hours always leaves you exhausted afterward.”
“Roma... you don't suspect I'm human?” Lu Mingfei ventured, thinking, Damn it, I am human, but please don't suspect it.
“How could you be?” Townsend dismissed the idea. “The screening here is strict. I haven't seen you before. New to the trade?”
“Oh, yes. My family's in building materials in China, and because I like...” Lu Mingfei hurriedly retrieved his cover story.

“The building materials business is very profitable in China!” Townsend exclaimed again. “My family's always been in construction too, but the golden age of North American construction is past. We can't possibly compete with Chinese real-estate developers.”
“Oh, come on, you imperialist countries...”
“But I hear in China you can even withhold workers' wages. How can we compete with that?” Townsend spread his hands.
Damn it! Lu Mingfei cursed inwardly. Word about migrant workers' unpaid wages had reached Lake Michigan. What a disgrace to the nation!
“Don't say too much. The more you say, the more likely you are to make a mistake.” Anjou's voice sounded in his ear. “Now it's time for a lesson from the principal himself.”

“You've always thought Cassell College was the only place where hybrids gather? Let me correct that. It's only one of them. You come from China, Caesar from Italy, Chu Zihang from China, Zero from Russia... Hybrids are spread across different parts of the world. Through marriage, dragon blood has traveled to every corner. We don't know how many hybrids exist worldwide. Those selected for Cassell College are only a tiny fraction. The others have their own ways of life, but because of their bloodlines they are drawn to one another and form a hidden sub-society within human society. What you're seeing now is hybrid society. It has its own rules.

“Cassell College grew out of the Dragon Blood Secret Party, whose aim is to destroy all pureblood dragons. But not every hybrid shares that ideal. More of them remain outside the war. They hate dragons, but don't consider themselves on humanity's side either. They believe their bloodlines are superior to humans', and call themselves a ‘third race’ between humans and dragons. Because of their blood, they age more slowly than ordinary people, and their aesthetic tastes lag behind too. Some of these people may already have been active in the middle of the last century. The flamboyant style of old Chicago is still fashionable among them.

“Some of their families have lasted for thousands of years, accumulating astonishing wealth and power. But because their positions differ, they won't necessarily support us. In any case, this is hybrid society: all kinds of people with all kinds of ideas, who need to communicate with one another. Auctions are one way they socialize. Do you remember what dragons' greatest obsession is said to be?”
“Stealing princesses?” How should I know, Lu Mingfei thought. Maybe you just like playing the villainous boss, kidnapping princesses in fairy tales and getting speared to death by knights.

“No. According to legend, dragons love collecting precious metals and gems, and sleep sprawled on gold,” Anjou said. “There's a basis for that. Dragons developed alchemy, and alchemy is the pinnacle of craftsmanship. Dragons are often obsessed with art. Attila, king of the Huns, for instance, was buried sealed in three coffins of gold, silver, and iron, each elaborately carved and set with gems. Hybrids inherited this obsession. Half the top collectors are hybrids, though you won't find their names in collecting magazines.”
“So they're artists too.” Lu Mingfei calmed down a little. He was already in the dragon's pool and tiger's den, but he at least understood the words accept your fate.

“The paddle in your hand is number seventeen, your birthday. All you have to do is raise it and bid in the most leisurely way possible. Ordinarily the increments don't need to be high, but a powerful buyer can intimidate others through sheer presence. When you think you need to win in one stroke, don't be afraid to make a large jump bid. It shows you're determined to have the item. Anyone bidding against you may hesitate: if they continue, the price could be driven too high, and they won't want to pay it. And if you're a plant for the auction house or another seller, they'll have fallen for it.”
“Presence is such an elusive thing...” Lu Mingfei whispered.
“Actually, in the way you young people put it...” Anjou chuckled. “Just act like a pompous badass.”

“Our next lot is a Qing Qianlong yangcai gourd vase with brocade-ground decoration and a longevity-and-ruyi motif. This porcelain from the Qianlong reign of the Qing dynasty represents the height of the ceramic art of its time, made for the imperial household by the Imperial Workshops. It left China after the Boxer War of 1900. A similar piece sold in Hong Kong for 17.3 million dollars a few months ago.” The auctioneer surveyed the room. “The opening bid is nine million dollars. Bids, please.”

This was the sixth lot of the day, and the opening price had risen from two hundred thousand to nine million. Lu Mingfei had not raised his paddle once, because Anjou had not given the order. Anjou himself, however, had bid on and won the great Nanyang Dushan jade vessel depicting Vairocana Buddha with lowered hands. Seated in the VIP section up front, he bid while whispering to the graceful young married woman beside him, looking perfectly content.
Now that was a pompous badass: bleeding money by the bucket while acting as if cash meant nothing, as if he'd come only for the love of art and to flirt with women! Lu Mingfei was impressed.

As opening prices climbed, the circle of competition narrowed to the VIP section. The earlier little pieces had been appetizers; this gourd vase was the main course, and several parties were fighting fiercely for it.

Anjou bid a few times, but he seemed merely bored and interested in driving up the price for others. Once it passed twenty million he withdrew and began telling jokes that made the young woman smile behind pursed lips.

Lu Mingfei grew bored. There was nothing special about this auction except that the participants were all hybrids. Everyone followed the rules, and so far no one had lost a bid, flown into a rage, and started blasting the others with Yanling. The game had gone beyond what he could play anyway: his mission budget was only two million.
“Twenty-three million one hundred thousand, going once!”
“Twenty-three million one hundred thousand, going twice! Last chance, please bid now.”
“Twenty-three million one hundred thousand, going three times! Sold!” The auctioneer brought down the hammer.
Polite applause filled the hall. The sale made a fine ending: the vase had been listed last in the catalog, the day's grand finale.
“Now for today's special segment, as always: ‘An Unexpected Encounter.’” The auctioneer smiled.
Lu Mingfei looked up in surprise and saw Townsend's eyes brighten.
“What encounter?” Lu Mingfei asked.
